A script as one expression

Source: R/script-expr.R
script_expr.Rd

The code a script block runs, built from the script alone: the controls are replaced by their values and the lines that declared them are gone. It is for a place that has the script but no block and no input, such as the call a report makes.

Usage

script_expr(script, values = list(), data = "data")

Arguments

script

The script, as for new_script_block().

values

Named list of control values, as a block's state holds them.

data

The name the expression reads the first input by. Every read of data in the script becomes a read of this name.

Value

An expression, or NULL when the script does not parse or has no statement left.

Details

A control takes its value from values, and the script's own value where values has none. Without an input, a declaration that reads the input, such as factor("a", levels = unique(data$col)), cannot be worked out. When values holds a value for it, that value is written in. When it does not, the line stays in the expression as code and is evaluated with the rest.

Examples

script_expr("n <- 6\n\nutils::head(data, n)", list(n = 3))
#> utils::head(data, 3)

# the levels need the input, the value comes from `values`
script_expr(
  "arm <- factor(\"A\", levels = unique(data$ARM))\nsubset(data, ARM == arm)",
  values = list(arm = "B"),
  data = "adsl"
)
#> subset(adsl, ARM == "B")
